items.notes: Mine and missile-range claims are IRGC statements; no independent confirmation of the mine strikes.
items.text: [[p:United States Central Command|CENTCOM]] set up Task Force Iron Gate on 7 Nov to disrupt Iranian arms and sanctioned trade over land borders and the Caspian Sea, beyond the naval blockade. The [[p:Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps|IRGC]] said it had lifted its self-imposed 2,000 km limit on missile range and that two tankers hit mines on an "unauthorised route" through Hormuz on 8 Nov; CENTCOM said it disabled a St Kitts-flagged ship in the Gulf of Oman. Iran is reviewing Qatari de-escalation proposals.

items.notes: Damage reported by witnesses; Saudi authorities had not commented on the tower.
items.text: The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed two [[p:Houthis|Houthi]] ballistic missiles fired at Riyadh on 8 Nov. Witnesses told AFP the Aramco tower in the [[p:King Abdullah Financial District]] was damaged, with shattered glass and part of its facade hit. No casualties were reported. The UN says more than 1,600 people have been killed since fighting resumed in Yemen.

items.notes: Missed by the 5 Nov Americas run. Vote count from a live blog; Infobae confirms resignation and Deputies impeachment vote. Logged Tier 2, so not in the brief.
items.text: Paraguay's Senate removed President [[p:Santiago Peña]] by impeachment on 6 Nov, 44 votes in favour, a day after he announced his resignation over the collapse of Ueno Bank, which the central bank had taken over. Vice-President [[p:Pedro Alliana]] was sworn in to finish the 2023–28 term. Prosecutors reportedly asked police to detain Peña; no arrest is confirmed.

items.notes: RTÉ gives United Serbia 104 seats; official RIK figure is 103.
items.text: Serbia's electoral commission confirmed the final [[e:2026 Serbian parliamentary election]] results on 5 Nov: the [[p:Student List]] won 140 of 250 seats, a clear majority, against 103 for [[p:Aleksandar Vučić]]'s United Serbia. Turnout was about 69%, the highest in over 30 years. The new assembly must sit within 30 days; cardiologist Ilija Srdanović is seen as the likeliest PM, and a presidential election is due by 27 Dec.
items.outlet: Government of Serbia (RIK report); Al Jazeera

items.text: The [[p:European Commission]]'s 2026 enlargement package (4 Nov) proposed membership roadmaps for Montenegro, Albania, Moldova and Ukraine. Montenegro could close all chapters by end-2026; Albania aims for 2027, Moldova early 2028 and Ukraine end-2028. Both Ukraine and Moldova meet the conditions to open all remaining clusters. Serbia made no substantive progress, Georgia's accession is de facto halted and Turkey's talks stay frozen.

Ukraine's EU envoy Taras Kachka said Hungary has raised "no substantive" new objections and only asked for more time on the documents, and expects clusters 4 and 5 to open by end-2026. Budapest has still not approved their screening reports.

After [[p:Donald Trump]] said a coming deal with Moscow "might involve all of Europe" and envoy [[p:Jared Kushner]] spoke of a new European security architecture, [[p:Kaja Kallas]] replied that Europe already has one and that [[p:Vladimir Putin]] has no veto over it. Poland's [[p:Radosław Sikorski]] called a deal "above our heads" impossible. Kushner promised Europeans consultation on the sidelines of the Abu Dhabi talks.

China's foreign ministry confirmed for the first time that it is "in communication" about a meeting of [[p:Xi Jinping]], Trump and Putin, likely on the sidelines of APEC in Shenzhen this month. Trump wants to discuss nuclear arms control; analysts quoted by the paper expect little beyond a photo opportunity.

items.notes: Kirill Dmitriev called the FT report "fake".
items.text: No Russian diesel has reached the US under Trump's deal: by 5 Nov the sanctioned tankers Talisman and Leruo had turned toward Brazil and the Mediterranean, and a third ship switched from New York to "for orders", after New Jersey's governor told terminals to turn the fuel away.

[[p:Christine Lagarde]] will step down as head of the [[p:European Central Bank]] on 7 Feb 2027, nine months early; no reason was given. The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.5% the same day, with euro-area inflation at 3.8% in September.

[[p:Ursula von der Leyen]] said Europe has paid an extra €127 billion for oil and gas since the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, for no extra energy. EU gas storage was about 74% on 3 Nov (Germany about 61%), roughly 12 points below the five-year norm and short of the relaxed 80% target.
items.outlet: Fortune; Global Energy Flow (GIE AGSI+ data)

items.text: In the eighth Security Council straw poll for UN Secretary-General on 5 Nov, [[p:Rebeca Grynspan]] got 12 "encourage" votes to 3 "discourage", ahead of [[p:Rafael Grossi]] (9–4). Ballots did not show permanent members' votes; colour-coded ballots may come next. Russia said it could look beyond Latin America.

EU budget talks: most capitals now accept they must agree the 2028–34 budget by end-2026, but [[p:António Costa]]'s negotiating box with figures is not expected before the last week of November. A deal at the 17–18 Dec summit is seen as likelier than at the 26 Nov extraordinary summit.

The UN climate conference COP31 opens in Antalya, Turkey, on 9 Nov and runs to 20 Nov, with Australia leading the negotiations under a Turkey–Australia arrangement. German Chancellor [[p:Friedrich Merz]] will not attend.

items.notes: PCh24 is a conservative outlet hostile to the government; rp.pl partly paywalled. "Forcible takeover" translated from Polish.
items.text: Poland's fight over the [[p:Constitutional Tribunal (Poland)|Constitutional Tribunal]] deepened. Judges elected by the current Sejm installed Anna Korwin-Piotrowska as acting head on 30 Oct and suspended president [[p:Bogdan Święczkowski]]; President [[p:Karol Nawrocki]] calls it a forcible takeover. On 6 Nov the Supreme Court declined to rule on the suspensions. A 17 Nov judges' assembly will weigh prosecutors' requests to lift Święczkowski's immunity and detain him.

France's National Assembly rejected the revenue part of the 2027 budget on 4 Nov with 458 votes against, killing the whole bill at first reading; the social-security budget fell on 23 Oct. Both go to the Senate unamended. PM [[p:Sébastien Lecornu]] could use Article 49.3, ordinances or a stopgap law.

The 5 Nov general strike drew 575,000 marchers by Interior Ministry count (1.6 million per the CGT), with 448 arrests and 53 officers injured. Lecornu called a "social conference" on wages with unions and employers for 9 Nov.

[[p:Iliana Iotova]] won Bulgaria's [[e:2026 Bulgarian presidential election|presidential runoff]] on 1 Nov with about 57% against Andrey Gyurov's 40%, becoming the first woman elected president. Turnout was a record low of about 29%.

[[p:Jimmie Åkesson]] dropped the [[p:Sweden Democrats]]' demand for cabinet posts and offered to back a four-party government under [[p:Ulf Kristersson]], who called this "less impossible". The Centre Party wants full programmes from both blocs. The Speaker extended Kristersson's exploration past 10 Nov.

items.notes: Polls are projections, not results. Election called 5 Oct; not logged by earlier runs.
items.text: Three weeks before Spain's 29 Nov snap election, called by [[p:Pedro Sánchez]] after Congress rejected his housing decrees, three late-October polls put the [[p:People's Party (Spain)|PP]] at 31–33% and [[p:Vox (political party)|Vox]] at 19–20%, together well above a majority, with the PSOE at 26–27%.
Bavaria's deputy premier and [[p:Free Voters]] leader [[p:Hubert Aiwanger]], 55, was found dead in a Berlin hotel; prosecutors say a preliminary autopsy found no sign of third-party involvement.
